items.title: Amulet of Entropy
items.maker: HackerBoxes / Carey Parker (Firewalls Don't Stop Dragons)
items.summary: An RP2040-based indie badge sold as HackerBox #0080 for DEF CON 30, with a round 240x240 IPS display, eight RGB LEDs, four buttons and four on-board entropy sources (ambient light, thermal noise, motion, semiconductor junction noise); hardware by HackerBoxes, software by Carey Parker.

results.notes: amuletofentropy.com is a minimal landing page that links out to the project's short write-up (firewallsdontstopdragons.com), a long-form podcast episode (Necessary Chaos, 2022-07-04), the hardware kit (HackerBox #0080 Entropy, $79, sold out) and the software repo (github.com/FirewallDragon/amulet-of-entropy). The repo README states it is an indie badge created for DEF CON 30 by HackerBoxes.com, developed over about 8 months, and was presented in a Crypto & Privacy Village talk; it credits Joe from HackerBoxes for the hardware and the author (Carey Parker) for the software design. The HackerBoxes store page credits Carey Parker's GitHub repo and links an Unbox & Build video by 463N7 (youtu.be/swqGDDqKy7U). Hardware: RP2040, 1.28-inch round 240x240 IPS display, 8 RGB LEDs, 4 buttons, LiPo manager, four entropy sources. This is the same item as existing entry dc30-amulet-of-entropy (listed there under maker HackerBoxes/bananajr); this page adds the Carey Parker / Firewalls Don't Stop Dragons attribution and the repo, store and guide links. The site returns HTTP 403 to curl (bot protection), which explains the fetch error in linkfile_meta.json; content was read via WebFetch. The amulet.png image URL is the page's relative image reference and was not independently verified due to the 403; the HackerBoxes product image URL is confirmed from the store page.

results.notes: GitHub repo (description "Etch A Sketch SAO") is the primary repository for one SAO, the Etch sAo Sketch by Andy Geppert (ageppert). An ePaper version is mentioned as planned but not built. Repo folders: Datasheets, Documentation, Electronic Design, Firmware, Images, Manufacturing, Mechanical Components. Errata: excess I2C pull-up resistance across all versions, fixed by removing R1/R2 (or R30/R31 on V1.0) or using software I2C. The README also mentions the maker's separate "SAO Demo Controller" host board (https://www.tindie.com/products/36033/) as a recommended host; it is a distinct item not documented on this page and has no existing archive entry, so a follow-up pass could catalogue it. All three candidate image URLs returned HTTP 200 (the Hackaday og:image https://cdn.hackaday.io/images/resize/600x600/8625281728913391740.jpeg is a third option).

results.page_title: astuder/duckglow: A set of basic SAOs with glowing rubber duckies

items.title: duckJAWS SAO
items.summary: A shark-shaped SAO from the duckGLOW family with a rubber duck lit by an RGB or UV LED plus side-lit red LEDs for the shark's teeth, driven by a CH32V003 and controllable over I2C or as a WS2812-style addressable LED, entered in the Supercon 8 SAO Contest and later sold assembled on Tindie.

items.title: duckBATH SAO
items.summary: A bathtub-shaped SAO from the duckGLOW family with a floating rubber duck lit by an RGB or UV LED, driven by a CH32V003 and controllable over I2C or as a WS2812-style addressable LED, designed for the Supercon 8 SAO Contest.

results.notes: GitHub repo (created 2024-10-14, last push 2025-01-13, language C) described as "A set of basic SAOs with glowing rubber duckies". duckGLOW is the umbrella name for the firmware and family; the repo holds two distinct KiCad PCB designs in folders duckjaws/ and duckbath/ (each with .kicad_pcb/.kicad_sch/.pdf), shared firmware in code/, artwork SVGs in design/, sample code in examples/ for the Supercon 8 SAO badge and Arduino, and photos/renders in pictures/ (duckjaws.jpg, duckbath.jpg, duckglow-both.jpg, renders). The README only names duckGLOW and the duckJAWS variant; the linked Hackaday.io project (created Oct 20, 2024, by Adrian Studer with team member Marc MERLIN) explicitly names both duckJAWS (shark nibbling the duck's tail, side-lit red LEDs) and duckBATH (bathtub for the floating duck) and states it was an entry in the Supercon 8 SAO Contest. The Tindie listing (seller Wegmatt LLC, Redmond WA, store https://www.tindie.com/stores/astuder/) says "as seen at Hackaday Supercon 2024", so event supercon-2024 is well supported for both boards. Common hardware: CH32V003 MCU, 3.3V boost converter, RGB common-anode or UV LED, four fading channels (R, G, B, background), default I2C address 0x6C selectable to 0x6F via solder jumpers, WS2812/NeoPixel mode. A third image showing both boards together is at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astuder/duckglow/master/pictures/duckglow-both.jpg. No existing archive entry matches (dc32-the-duck-badge is a different Red String Studio item). Same maker also has the repo astuder/supercon8-sao-adapters in linkfile_meta.json, which is a separate intake item.

items.title: Bob Ross Happy Trees SAO
items.summary: A purely decorative AND!XOR SAO for DEF CON 27 that does nothing electrically except frame another SAO, with a zip-tie hole for mounting to a badge; Gerbers are in the repo and it was shared on OSH Park.

items.title: DC619 EEPROM SAO
items.summary: A simple I2C EEPROM SAO (AT24-family chip at address 0x50) that AND!XOR published for DEF CON 27 as the reference for their proposed EEPROM data format of DC year, maker ID, SAO type ID, then arbitrary data.

items.title: GPIO 16 (MCP23017) reference design
items.summary: A 16-LED SAO driven by an MCP23017 I2C GPIO expander at address 0x20, published by AND!XOR for DEF CON 27; their badge plays special patterns when it detects the chip on the bus, a behaviour carried over from DEF CON 26.

items.title: Shitty Brooch
items.summary: A lapel-pin brooch with a CR2032 holder and 2x3 female header that powers an SAO without a badge, published by AND!XOR for DEF CON 27 with schematic and Gerbers.

results.notes: The ANDnXOR/sao-reference-designs URL now redirects to zapp1337/sao-reference-designs (same repo, moved; not a fork; Apache-2.0; last push 2019-04-20, before DEF CON 27). Repo description: "AND!XOR Reference Designs for SAOs". Structure: root README, LICENSE, and a single DC27/ folder holding four designs, all using the SAO 1.69bis connector. Classification tension: the repo frames itself as reference designs (which the intake rules map to "reference"), but the four folders are concrete, named boards from a known badge maker for a specific event, and one (Bob Ross Happy Trees) is a finished decorative SAO shared for ordering on OSH Park, so I classified it as a collection; a reviewer could reasonably downgrade the EEPROM and GPIO-16 entries to reference-only since their READMEs read as generic building blocks. Event is explicit: folder is DC27 and the root README says to use 0x1B for DC27; GPIO folder says the MCP23017 SAOs are "returning from DC26", so that design also existed at DC26. Titles: "Bob Ross Happy Trees SAO" and "Shitty Brooch" and "GPIO 16 (MCP23017) reference design" are the READMEs' verbatim H1s; the EEPROM folder README has only "I2C" and "EEPROM" headings, so "DC619 EEPROM SAO" is derived from the folder name DC619-EEPROM_sao1.69bis (DC619 is not explained on the page; it may be a DEF CON group reference but that is inference, not page content). Discrepancy: root README says the EEPROM is an AT24C32, the folder README says AT24C02N. The root README also lists a third "REDACTED" I2C device type with address TBD, never published here. Maker ID convention noted: AND!XOR uses 0x49. No existing archive entry matched (no dc27 entries and nothing for Bob Ross, brooch, EEPROM, or MCP23017); the AND!XOR entries in the archive are dc30 through dc33 badges. The OSH Park link returned an empty page with no og:image, so the Bob Ross item has no image URL; the other three image URLs are schematics or a rendered PNG from the repo rather than photos of assembled boards. maker_url is the GitHub org since the page gives no other maker link.

PCBs were green JLCPCB boards for fastest turnaround; no store link. (Nanik Adnani), Yo Dawg (davedarko), Infinity Mirror (Scorch Works), Wolverine (Simen E. Sørensen). None of these, nor the adapters, matched anything in existing_titles.txt. items.title: Supercon Add-On Badge
items.summary: The official Hackaday Supercon 8 (2024) badge: a hub for six SAO ports built around a MicroPython-running microcontroller, designed so attendees combine I2C add-ons and can program a CH32V003 proto petal directly from the badge.

items.title: Spiral Matrix Petal
items.summary: An LED-matrix SAO shipped with the Supercon 8 badge (repo folder and BOM call it Petal Matrix), driven by an AS1115 I2C display driver with an RGB LED at the center.

items.title: Pure Proto Petal

items.summary: A CH32V003-based prototyping SAO for the Supercon 8 badge that can be configured as an arbitrary I2C device, with all chip I/O broken out, a debug LED on PD0, and a Program jumper so the badge itself can flash it.

items.title: Touchwheel SAO
items.summary: A capacitive touch-wheel SAO by todbot (ATtiny816 firmware, I2C memory-map interface) that was distributed with the Supercon 8 badge and is included in the badge repo as a git submodule.

results.notes: The URL is astuder's fork of Hack-a-Day/2024-Supercon-8-Add-On-Badge. GitHub compare shows the fork is 0 commits ahead and 59 behind upstream (last push 2024-11-02), so it contains nothing of astuder's own; the repo owner (astuder) is not the maker and the canonical source is the upstream Hack-a-Day repo. The fork's README is a single line, "2024 Supercon 8 -- Supercon Add-On Badge", plus a glamour shot; item details come from the sub-READMEs in the fork (hardware/sao/petal_matrix, pure_proto_petal, i2c_proto_petal) and the upstream README, which names the LED petal, Touchwheel petal, and the CH32V003 protoboard as add-ons that come with the badge. The upstream README title has since been extended to "2025 Hackaday Europe -- Simple Add-On Badge" (the badge was reused there), but the fork only references Supercon 8, so items are filed under supercon-2024. No designer credit appears in the repo, so maker is recorded as Hackaday. The Touchwheel SAO is an external todbot project pulled in as a submodule; confidence medium on treating it as a Supercon 2024 item, though the README explicitly says the Touchwheel petal ships with the badge. Badge hardware files are CircuitStudio (.CSPcbDoc) plus PDF/PS schematics and a combined Badge_2024_and_Petal_Matrix_BOM.xlsx; the I2C proto petal is a KiCad project. Related URLs already present in linkfile_meta.json that should be processed separately: https://github.com/astuder/supercon8-sao-adapters and https://github.com/astuder/duckglow. No existing archive entries match any of these items (no supercon-2024 ids and no petal/touchwheel/add-on-badge titles in existing_titles.txt).

results.page_title: GitHub - cryptovillage/badge2015: Hardware, firmware, and documentation for the 2015 Crypto and Privacy Village Badge

items.title: DEF CON 23 Crypto and Privacy Village Badge
items.maker: Crypto and Privacy Village (Karl Koscher, Jorge Lacoste)
items.summary: The Crypto and Privacy Village's DEF CON 23 (2015) village badge: an MSP430G2955 board with a 7-segment display, twelve green LEDs and buttons, running Energia firmware with twelve flag challenges hashed by 3000 rounds of XXTEA, plus easter eggs including a Baudot LED mode, a party mode, and a Tetris mode that broadcasts the Tetris theme over AM radio by modulating an LED.

results.notes: Repo owned by the cryptovillage GitHub org, described as "Hardware, firmware, and documentation for the 2015 Crypto and Privacy Village Badge". Folders: docs/ (design document "DC23CPV Badge No Flags" as .docx and .pdf), firmware/cpvfinal/ (Energia/Arduino-style firmware for MSP430G2955), hw/ (KiCad project badge2015.sch/.kicad_pcb plus schematic.pdf), tools/ (genflag/genegg flag-hashing utilities). Only two commits, both 2015-09-27 by Karl Koscher (GitHub supersat); LICENSE is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2015 Jorge Lacoste and Karl Koscher", so those two are the credited makers under the village. The design document's own heading reads "DEF CON 23 Crypto And Privacy Village Badge Design Document" and the display cycles "DEFCON23 / CRYPTO / AND / PRIVACY / VILLAGE", which fixes the event as DEF CON 23 (2015); dc23 is not in events.yml (earliest is dc24), hence the new_event proposal. Note the WebFetch summarizer mislabelled the PDF as a "DEFCON 27" badge; the extracted PDF text says DEF CON 23 throughout, so that summary was wrong. Features from the design doc: self-test mode, display mode with 12 challenge LEDs, flag entry via up/down/left/right buttons, easter eggs (Matrix, LED1, LED2, Count, Pong, EFF donor "I fight for the users" message, Baudot "LOOK IN TO MY EYES" mode, Tetris/RF mode at 550 kHz AM followed by Morse at 15 WPM, party/rager mode at 128 BPM, "fuck"/"sorry" lockout, bullet time, "factoryr" NVM reset). An unpopulated footprint was for a digital compass dropped before manufacture. No photos of the badge exist in the repo or PDF (pdfimages found none) and the GitHub og:image is only a repository card, so image_urls is left empty. Existing entry dc24-cpv-badge is the following year's CPV badge, a different item, so existing_entry_id is empty.

This repo is the static-site archive of the Crypto & Privacy Village "Gold Bug" cryptography puzzle challenge run at DEF CON, not a badge or SAO. It has no README and no repo description (linkfile_meta: description null, homepage null, 6 stars, last push 2025-02-09). Top level is year folders 2015, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 plus themed puzzle-year folders CirqueMystique, HelloNeighbor, SeekTheJabberwock, WelcomeToTheArcade and a root index.html. Each year folder holds puzzle pages (e.g. 2015 compass-direction puzzles and an r00tzcryptochallenge page; 2018 puzzles such as Hut8, Polyglot, CryptoFactzors, AgentProvocateur, TalkShowHost with an mp3). No KiCad, gerber, firmware or hardware design files. The only badge-adjacent content is 2018/textures/badge2018-*.svg (F.Cu, B.Cu, In1.Cu, In2.Cu, SilkS, Edge.Cuts layer renders of a 2018 badge, used as three.js textures for a puzzle) which appears to depict the Crypto & Privacy Village DC26 (2018) badge; there is no matching DC26 CPV badge entry in existing_titles (only dc24-cpv-badge exists, maker Crypto & Privacy Village), so a later pass could use this as a pointer that a CPV 2018 badge exists, but this repo does not document it as an item. No og:image, store, or badge repo links found. Index pages render almost entirely via JavaScript so the text extraction was empty; the folder tree is the evidence.

items.title: Crypto & Privacy Village DC26 Badge
items.summary: The official Crypto & Privacy Village badge for DEF CON 26 (2018), a gold-plated ESP32 + EFM8UB1 'split-brained' badge with RGB LEDs, capacitive touch pads, LiPo/micro-USB power, a DC26 Shitty Add-On header, and a built-in hardware challenge tied to the village's Gold Bug puzzle; this repo holds its KiCad hardware, ESP32 and EFM8 firmware, emulator, OTA server, and tools.

results.notes: Single-badge source repo (no description, 3 commits, last push 2019-06-09, 17 stars). Repo never states the event by name, but three independent signals fix it as DEF CON 26 / 2018: the repo name badge2018 and firmware hwconf 'cpv18', the KiCad footprint hardware/lib/DC26_Shitty_Addon.kicad_mod (SAO v1 header on the badge), and Hackaday's 'All The Badges Of DEF CON 26 (vol 3)' article, which covers this badge and links this repo. Hackaday and the DEF CON 26 villages page describe it as the official CPV badge: ESP32 + EFM8 dual-MCU, gold-plated copper with solder-mask lettering, RGB LEDs on the front, capacitive touch pads, LiPo with micro-USB charging, tessellating outline, and a hardware challenge tied to the Gold Bug puzzle (goldbug.cryptovillage.org). The SAO footprint is a header on the badge, not a separate add-on, so this is one item, not a collection. items.title: DC34 Mech SAO (weapon plug-ins)
items.summary: A family of five weapon-themed SAO plug-in boards (missile, gatling, laser, fist, sword) for the CPEC DEF CON 34 Mech Badge; each runs the same ATtiny816 Adafruit-seesaw I2C firmware with its identity set by onboard resistors, so the ESP32 badge can hot-detect which weapon is plugged into each of its three SAO slots.

results.notes:
GitHub repo (not a fork, not archived, last push 2026-07-16, i.e. a few weeks before DEF CON 34 on Aug 6-9 2026). Repo description: "Kicad 6 design files for the CPEC DEFCON 34 Badge SAO pluggin weapon and power ups." README says the boards are SAO plug-in modules for the CPEC DC 34 badge and points to the firmware/host demo at eggsactly/DcC4-Mech-SAO-Plugin-Demo (the org also mirrors it as DC-34-Mech-SAO-Plugin-Demo).

File tree shows five distinct KiCad board designs under DC34-Mech-SAO/: missile-00, gatling-01, laser-02, fist-03, sword-04, plus a shared panel file, one JLCPCB BOM/CPL pair named "DC-34-CPEC-Mech-SAO-Rev01p1", and one Arduino sketch (DC34-Mech-SAO-Firmware.ino). The sketch header states all boards take the exact same program and are configured by resistors on each board; it is an Adafruit seesaw peripheral on an ATtiny816 (I2C addr 0x49, up to 3 addresses via ADDR pins, NeoPixel/PWM/ADC enabled, UPDI programmed). The host demo (ESP32, 240 MHz) polls three SAO slots with a query_sao() library and prints the weapon name, e.g. "SAO 1: laser 4". Artis_art/ holds SVG art for fist, laser, machine_gun, missile_launcher, sword, plus a CPEC logo and perforation outlines. Only weapons appear in the files; no "power up" boards exist despite the description, so that wording is aspirational or unfinished.

Reported as ONE grouped item because the five boards share a single BOM, firmware, panel and revision, and the archive already groups SAO families (cf. dc34-badgelife-village-saos). If a later pass prefers one entry per weapon, the maker's own names are DC34-Mech-SAO-missile-00, -gatling-01, -laser-02, -fist-03, -sword-04.

Image URLs are raw SVG design art (no photos exist in either repo; the demo repo's images/ folder only has a Fritzing breadboard sketch). No og:image beyond GitHub's generic card.

Related CPEC DC34 repos seen on the org page, none yet in the archive and worth separate intake: DC34-Mech-Badge ("DEFCON 34 Mech Badge by CPEC", the host badge, ESP32 with Crystalfontz CFAF240320A0 display per DC-34-Display), DC-34-Badge (CPEC Badge KiCad files for DEF CON 34), DC34-CPEC-SAO ("SAO Design for DC34"), DC34-CPEC-The-Cheat ("The Cheat" SAO board), DC34-Mech-Badge-Game, and DC32-SAO (SAO for DEF CON 32). No existing_titles match for CPEC, Cyber Professionals, Mech, missile, weapon or power-up.

items.title: 2026 iFixit SAO
items.maker: iFixit, Cal Poly NerdFlare club, and znjp
items.summary: PCB-art SAO shaped like a raised fist holding a soldering iron, made for DEF CON 2026 (DC34) as a collaboration between iFixit, the Cal Poly NerdFlare club and znjp; an ATtiny1604 drives seven SK6805 addressable LEDs along the iron shaft, a red tip LED and two lightning-bolt LEDs, with Off/Candle/Propane animation modes plus a locked mode unlocked by soldering four 0-ohm resistors (1206/0805/0603/0402) onto challenge footprints, and the firmware is a PlatformIO/Arduino project programmable over UPDI.

results.notes: GitHub repo (description "iFixit DEFCON 2026 SAO", last pushed 2026-07-24, folders art/, code/, pcb/, images/) holding firmware, KiCad/PCB files and artwork for one SAO. README credits "iFixit, the Cal Poly NerdFlare club, and znjp". Event: the repo says only "DEFCON 2026"; DEF CON 34 is the 2026 DEF CON (events.yml dc34, Aug 6-9 2026), so event=dc34. Hardware per README: ATtiny1604-SS, 7x SK6805-EC15 LEDs (iron shaft), 1x 0402 red tip LED, 2x reverse-mount gull-wing LEDs (lightning bolt), rear mode button, exposed 2.54mm UPDI pads, standard 2x3 SAO header. Checked against existing entry dc34-badgelife-village-saos (Level 1/2/3 learn-to-solder kits, designers Ozma of Oz + GhostGlitch, iFixit as sponsor): compared photos, the Level 3 board is a round white DEF CON smiley/crossbones SAO, while this repo's board is a fist-and-soldering-iron shape, so they are different items and existing_entry_id is left empty. This SAO is likely related to iFixit's DC34 Badgelife Village sponsorship but the repo does not say where or how it was distributed. Image URLs verified returning 200 image/jpeg on the main branch. Also in repo: images/ifixit-2026-operation.gif and images/updi.jpg. Fetch/search calls used: 6.

items.title: Badgerunner
items.summary: A Blade Runner-themed badge for Hackaday Supercon 2019 shaped like the Tyrell Corporation's owl, with an ESP12 driving nine NeoPixels (eight on the front flashing a hidden message, one reversed to backlight the cybernetic eye), LiPo power with micro-USB charging, and an SAO header on each ear.

results.notes: The GitHub repo itself is thin: a one-line README ("Bladerunner themed conference badge designed like the classic Bladerunner replicant Owl"), an Arduino sketch (badgerunner0.1.ino), a KiCad project under pcb/ (art.kicad_pcb, built with svg2shenzhen), art/ (art.svg, edgeCuts.dxf), ref/ (ESP32 datasheets and a Shutterstock owl reference image), a badgerunner_final.zip, and a Google Doc pointer that cannot be fetched. Repo description on GitHub: "Bladerunner badge"; last push 2019-09-23; no license, no topics, no photos of the finished badge in the repo (GitHub og:image is just the auto-generated card). The event and year do not appear in the repo; they come from the directly linked Hackaday.io project "BADGE RUNNER" (project 168402) by Claire Sun (csun.codes), which names this repo as the project's GitHub and states it was made for Hackaday Superconference 2019 (held near LA in Nov 2019, matching the film's setting), that multiple units were built to sell at Supercon with leftovers headed to Tindie, and links a programmer under sphawes/glowtie. Repo owner sphawes is Stephen Hawes (display name confirmed on his GitHub profile), so the maker is listed as both. The Hackaday.io page calls the MCU an ESP12 while the repo's ref/ folder holds ESP32/ESP32-CAM datasheets; treat the exact MCU as unverified. Image URLs are the Hackaday.io og:image and cover image. No existing archive entry matched badgerunner, bladerunner, owl, hawes, or sun. No new_event needed since supercon-2019 already exists in events.yml.

items.title: Mr Fixit
items.summary: A single-LED art SAO by Tom Keddie shaped like a cartoon repairman in red solder mask with a gold HASL outline, whose handheld multimeter display lights up from the SAO connector's 3.3 V rail; first designed and manufactured in November 2019 (v1.0/v1.1) and re-spun as rev 1.3 in September 2024.

results.notes: The URL is one folder ("mr-fixit") inside Tom Keddie's prj-pcb-experiments KiCad repo (BSD-2-Clause, 4 stars, last push 2025-08-31). There is no README at the folder or root level (root README is just the line "# tom-pcb-experiments"), so all facts come from the KiCad files, commit log and images. Evidence it is an SAO: the schematic/PCB use the footprint "tom-connectors:PinSocket_2x03_P2.54mm_Vertical_SMD_SAO" (J1, Conn_02x03_Odd_Even) plus one LED (D1, XZM2CYK45WT-9 no-mask footprint) and a 220R resistor (R1) between +3.3V and GND; the artwork is carried as copper/mask/silk footprints in mr-fixit.pretty. The Dec 2019 photo shows a red-mask, gold-outlined repairman figure with a wrench in his pocket holding a multimeter whose display window is the lit LED; the artwork PNG is a silhouette of the same figure. Silkscreen text on the current PCB reads "tom@tomk.in v1.3 Sep2025 @TomKeddie JLCJLCJLCJLC" (JLCPCB order marker). Commit history: 2019-11-22 graphics, first pass, copper layers, "v1.0 as submitted, hasl copper outline with red mask internal + multimeter led"; 2019-11-26 "v1.1 edge cuts changes as v1.0 failed audit" and v1.1 gerber zip; 2019-12-13 photos added; 2024-09-16 "mrfixit: rev1.3 as sent for mfg" (matches the 2024-09-16 gerber zip filenames). Note the silkscreen says "Sep2025" while the commit and zip dates say Sept 2024; treat the year of rev 1.3 as 2024 with the silk text likely a typo, or possibly a later uncommitted edit. Year given as 2019 (first manufactured); the 2024 rev could alternatively be catalogued. No conference or event is named anywhere in the folder, commits or files, so event is "other" and confidence is medium; timing of the Sept 2024 re-spin is consistent with Supercon 2024 (the same repo has a "2024-supercon-sign-sao" folder) but that is inference, not stated. No existing archive entry matches (the only "fixit" hit, dc34-badgelife-village-saos, is an iFixit-made SAO by different makers). Web search was unavailable (session search budget exhausted). For a later pass: the parent repo holds other likely badge/SAO folders worth their own intake — 2024-rfid-sao, 2024-supercon-sign-sao, peace-sign-sao, snoopy-sao, covid-dude, covid-mask, skull-roses, east-van, big-clive, strange-parts, deutsche-bahn, baggage-label, kindcalmsafe, 2025-mini-keychain, 2025-flex-spiral, and the xmas-tree/ball/snowflake boards.

This is the canonical Shitty Add-On (SAO) specification page on Hackaday.io, authored by Benchoff (Brian Benchoff, https://hackaday.io/hacker/7-benchoff) with about 20 listed contributors. It is a standard/spec, not a specific badge or SAO, so page_kind is reference and no items are listed. Content: the community-derived SAO standard for attaching small add-on PCBs to conference badges; the current text documents SAO V1.69bis (2x3 0.1" header, 3.3V power, two GPIO pins suitable for WS2812/APA102 LED strings, 3.6V signal max, 330 ohm minimum series resistor on GPIO). It cites DEF CON 25 and DEF CON 26 as the origin context, DC27 for v1.69bis, and references prior art in the SaintCon MiniBadge standard (SaintCon 2017) and the 2016 Queercon badge expansion ports. Reference hardware mentioned on the page (not catalogued as items because they are dev/reference tools, not conference SAOs): the "Shitty Add-On Developer's Platform" (a Raspberry Pi HAT) and the "DC26 Shitty Development Board". items.title: Sloth Badge

results.notes: Single-item Hackaday.io project page by davedarko (Berlin, Germany; "team of 1"). Project created 2017-11-24 as a Coin Cell Challenge entry; production run announced 2018-01-01, redesigned 2018-02-20 after the Pimoroni design-rights arrangement fell through (the original was a direct nod to Pimoroni's Bearables bear/fox badges, with the designer's initial blessing). items.title: Furbymin Defcon 27 SOA
items.summary: An Area 51-themed DEF CON 27 SAO shaped like a lobotomized Furby that works as a dual photoresistive theremin with capacitive touch pads to modify the sound, switched on by touching the beak, using 2 of 6 available oscillators with a spring-jack spot on one ear for a signal out to a modular synth and a raid meme on the back.

results.notes: Live PCBWay shared-project page, posted 2019-11-24, licensed CC BY-SA 3.0. PCBWay author is listed as "Andrew nicholson" (USA) with "Kathryn Fortunato" (USA) shown as a collaborator; the member profile has no bio, links, or other posts. The same board is sold on Tindie as "Red Furbymin Theremin SOA DC27 (full assembled)" for $30 by the store Harbinger LTD (Tindie handle awkwardai, Atlanta, GA), which is why the maker is given as Harbinger LTD (Andrew Nicholson). Tindie listing says the store is "On A Break"; the store index page itself is Cloudflare-blocked (HTTP 403) so a full product list could not be read.
